fact_text: Pakistan's tractor industry volumes have been broadly stagnant, with a negative compound growth rate from 2016 onwards, mirroring the flat trend in local car volumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Millat Tractors' profit before tax per tractor rose from about PKR 150,000 in FY2016 to roughly PKR 600,000-700,000 by 2026, even though industry volumes did not grow.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Roughly two out of every three tractors sold in Pakistan are Millat units, and the company's tractors are built under a Massey Ferguson collaboration.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In May 2026 a Millat Tractors subsidiary signed a memorandum with a Chinese electric two-wheeler maker to assemble, manufacture and market electric bikes in Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Millat's electric-bike venture starts by importing completely-built-up units, with letters of credit opened, to test which models sell, before moving to completely-knocked-down local assembly; dealer onboarding has begun.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst screens a two-wheeler product on four criteria - features, battery range, price and reliability - the same way he ranks cars, to judge whether it can take share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes that a cheap electric bike is not enough to win in Pakistan: warranty, reliability, spare-part availability and after-sales service decide whether a new entrant holds share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: About 200,000 electric scooters were sold in Pakistan in the first nine months of 2026, implying an annual run-rate around 270,000 units.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Expensive petrol, better electric models and government support including the Punjab chief minister's e-bike scheme are the three drivers the analyst credits for Pakistan's electric two-wheeler adoption.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In an illustrative case the analyst sized the electric-bike venture at 100,000 units a year on a 500,000-unit market and 20% share, about PKR 250 billion of revenue at a PKR 250,000 average price and a 10% net margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On those illustrative electric-bike assumptions the analyst saw roughly PKR 2 billion of after-tax profit, adding around PKR 5 to Millat's earnings per share, but stressed these are projections to be monitored.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst projected Millat selling about 25,000 tractors in FY27 on a 60-65% market share, with better wheat prices and no floods supporting farm economics and a 20,000-unit government scheme inside industry demand.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On 25,000 tractors the analyst modelled Millat revenue of PKR 90-95 billion, gross profit near PKR 25 billion, operating profit near PKR 20 billion and after-tax profit of PKR 10-12 billion in FY27.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: That FY27 profit scenario translates to earnings per share of roughly PKR 23-27 for Millat Tractors, against a historical multiple of about 11 times earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With a near-100% payout maintained, the analyst expected about PKR 25-30 of dividend per share for FY27, a dividend yield of roughly 9-10%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: By FY26 Millat's profit per tractor stood roughly 50% above Al-Ghazi's, which the analyst attributed to economies of scale and slightly deeper localisation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Millat trades at a price-to-earnings ratio roughly 40-50% above Al-Ghazi's, which the analyst links to its longer dividend and compounding record and the resulting investor trust.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst tests the roughly five-times market-cap gap between Millat and Al-Ghazi against four factors: double the volumes, higher profit per tractor, a premium multiple, and the new electric-bike project.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Millat has signed a distribution partnership with Weichai Lovol Intelligent Agriculture Technology of China, giving it access to farm machinery it could import and supply as corporate farming grows in Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The draft auto policy would raise customs duty on imported built-up conventional tractors from 10% to 15% by 2031 and on built-up electric tractors from zero to 5%, leaving knocked-down duties unchanged.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because knocked-down tractor duties are untouched in the draft auto policy, the analyst expects almost no impact on local tractor makers, unlike cars and bikes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Tractor sales are highly seasonal and unevenly spread across quarters, so the analyst reads any Millat quarterly result against the tractor units delivered in that quarter before judging profitability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's stated process is a three-step sequence - understand the business, verify the numbers, then invest - rather than acting on a recommendation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's key lesson from Millat is that a company can compound shareholder wealth by lifting profit per unit on flat volumes, so unit growth is not a precondition for a multibagger.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Millat Tractors: 100% Dividend Payout & A New Growth Story?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
